title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 14 close: Peter to heaven — same will, diverse habitude; Papist case ends
pass_a_gloss: Let us accommodate these things to our purpose: God intends to send Peter across into Heaven: he wills this earlier than he decrees efficacious and infallible means for him: for he would never have established to supply such means to him, unless he had earlier efficaciously decreed to give him heavenly glory. But now let it descend to execution: God wills that he first become a partaker of grace, from grace work well, persevere in good works unto the end, before he puts in at the harbor of heavenly glory. Here if some Jesuit disputant rise up and cry out that God has changed his will, because from the beginning he intended glory for Peter earlier than grace or perseverance in good works, and now wills on the contrary that he first be imbued with grace and walk perseveringly in good works before he arrives at glory, I will laugh at the man's ineptitudes, and will say that this diverse consideration, as to intention and production of the same thing, does not posit in God a diverse or changeable will, but a diverse habitude of the same will toward the same thing under diverse considerations. These are nearly those things which are disputed by the Papists for election from foreseen works.
pass_b_english: Fit this to our case: God intends to send Peter into Heaven — he wills that before he decrees efficacious, infallible means for him; he would never have resolved to supply such means unless he had first efficaciously decreed to give him heavenly glory. At execution God wills that Peter first share in grace, work well from grace, and persevere in good works to the end, before he makes harbor at heavenly glory. If some Jesuit disputant rises and shouts that God changed his will — because at first he intended glory for Peter before grace or perseverance, and now wills the reverse, grace and persevering good works before glory — I will laugh at the man's folly, and say this diverse consideration of intention and production of the same thing does not posit a diverse or changeable will in God, but a diverse habitude of the same will toward the same thing under diverse considerations. That is nearly all the Papists dispute for election from foreseen works.
source_text: Accommodemus haec instituto nostro: Deus intendit Petrum in Caelum transmittere: prius hoc vult quam media efficacia et infallibilia illi decernit: nunquam enim statuisset talia media illi suppeditare, nisi prius efficaciter decrevisset caelestem gloriam illi donare. Verum jam ad exsecutionem descendatur, Deus vult ut prius gratiae particeps fiat, ex gratia bene operetur, in bonis operibus ad finem usque perseveret, quam ad portum caelestis gloriae appellat. Hic si Jesuiticus aliquis disputator insurgat et vociferetur, Deum mutasse voluntatem suam, quia ab initio prius intendebat Petro gloriam quam gratiam aut perseverantiam in bonis operibus, nunc vult e contra ut prius gratia imbuatur, et in bonis operibus perseveranter ambulet, quam ad gloriam perveniat, ridebo hominis ineptias, et dicam diversam hanc considerationem, quoad intentionem et productionem ejusdem rei, non ponere in Deo diversam aut mutabilem voluntatem, sed ejusdem voluntatis ad eandem rem sub diversis considerationibus diversam habitudinem. Haec fere ea sunt quae a Papistis disputantur pro electione ex praevisis operibus.
